changelog: Storage-card health checks now run between restarts: the card is checked every hour and a small write test runs once a day, so a card that starts failing is noticed the same day instead of at the next restart. If a software update is offered while the card is already reporting a problem, the system now warns you not to install it yet: you get an on-screen notice saying so, and Cytech is emailed automatically -- an update writes a large amount of data and could make a failing card worse. When the card is healthy, nothing changes and no warning appears. Alert-email setup is now fully automatic: a new system installs its email account by itself, and if you press Register before that has finished, it simply tells you to try again in a few minutes -- no installer visit is ever needed.
details: v52a (BENCH ROUND -- local commits only, nothing pushed). SD-card early warning + update gate. Four files changed. (1) packages/cytech.yaml. New template binary_sensor binary_sensor.cytech_sd_trouble (unique_id cytech_sd_trouble_sensor, device_class problem) ORs the four trouble signals: sensor.cytech_sd_card_status == FAIL, sensor.cytech_sd_canary == FAIL, sensor.cytech_warning == REPEATED_RESTARTS, sensor.cytech_integrity_alert not in ('', unknown, unavailable) -- the gate and its warning text can never disagree about what counts. The card checks no longer run only at HA start: new automation cytech_periodic_sd_check (time_pattern minutes '23' -- hourly kernel-log scan, deliberately off the hour so it never stacks with the on-the-hour 4-hourly eth/config checks) reruns cytech_check_sdcard, and new cytech_periodic_canary (daily 03:41) reruns the 8 MB write/readback test (extra wear stays at canary scale, ~8 MB/day). New automation cytech_update_hold_on_offer: a template trigger that fires only on its expression turning true (no from_state bookkeeping), testing is_state(... 'on') for both update-entity id vintages in the fleet (older registrations keep update.home_assistant_core, newer ones have ..._core_update; entity ids pin at first registration, the v42b lesson; ids that do not exist simply read false; no regex -- Jinja has no 'search' test, caught offline). On a fresh offer it first RERUNS both card checks and waits 2 minutes (scripts fork; covers SSH-retry slow paths plus the 60 s command_line re-scan), so the gate judges the CURRENT card, not a stale morning result; then acts only while binary_sensor.cytech_sd_trouble is on. New automation cytech_update_hold_on_trouble covers the mirror case (trouble appears while an offer is already sitting un-pressed) with the same is_state offer condition and no fresh-check preamble. Both end in new script script.cytech_update_hold_notify: creates the persistent notification (id cytech_update_hold, title 'Do not install the update yet -- storage card problem detected', message carries the failing check's own text in the same priority order as the mailer) and calls the new INLINE shell_command cytech_alert_mail_updatehold. The gate can only warn -- HA offers no way to block Supervisor installing its own update -- and deliberately sends nothing when trouble appears with NO update offered: the v35/v42 alerts already mailed. (2) cytech_alert_mail.py: new kind updatehold, no result file of its own -- gate_message() composes the body from the troubled card-check files in priority order (sdcard FAIL, canary FAIL, boot storm REPEATED_RESTARTS, integrity) and falls through to the generic advice on missing/garbled files; copies follow the v41 rule (support always, owner when registered); subject 'Cytech: do not install the pending update: <unit>'. (3) cytech_check_sdcard.sh and cytech_canary.sh: header comments only (schedule now includes the periodic automations). Offline verification: YAML parse + structure asserts; all four new templates parsed AND rendered against mocked state layers (offer-check 12 cases incl. both id vintages, off, unavailable, unrelated addon update, none; sd_trouble 8 cases incl. SKIP and integrity-ts); mailer fixture suite 17/17 (priority order, generic fallback, garbled files, support-only, rc=2 no creds, legacy sdcard regression); bash -n on both scripts. Bench verification: PASSED on ems.local 2026-10-15 via a real Check -> Update Now from a local mirror (27/27 deployed-file md5s = committed blobs, core auto-restarted, version 52a, pending cleared). T1: new entities/automations loaded; sd_trouble off on the healthy card; an already-true offer template at restart did NOT fire (transition-only, as designed). Healthy offer: on_offer fired 12:44:28Z, reran both card checks 12:44:30, silent -- no notification, no mail. Trouble with no offer: injected FAIL -> sd_trouble on 12:49:23, v35 sdcard alert mailed 20:49:30, gate silent (on_trouble condition-blocked; noted: blocked runs leave no logbook entry and no last_triggered update). Trouble appears while an offer is pending: on_trouble fired 12:56:23Z -> sdcard + updatehold mails 20:56:30. Stale injected FAIL + offer: the gate's own fresh checks overwrote the stale file and the gate stayed silent -- it judges the CURRENT card. Injected FAIL (stub script with the real runner shape) + offer transition: on_offer 13:01:52 + on_trouble 13:02:23, mails 21:02:31 (sdcard) + 21:02:33 (updatehold, immediate path) + 21:03:59 (updatehold, after the on_offer 2-min gate); alerts log 4 -> 7, every line rc=0 support=sent owner=sent. A natural coordinator refresh mid-round restored the real offer-entity states and on_offer ran silently on the healthy card (unplanned at-rest evidence). Periodic automations manually triggered: both fired, fresh sdcard + canary OK lines logged. Teardown: real check script restored (md5 d26e21d7fe22297a6b2813f7f14a8c90), .cytech_secrets back on the fleet GitHub URL, offer overrides refreshed, notifications dismissed, final snapshot version 52a / sd_trouble off / all sensors OK / no pending. (52c addition, same bench round.) Alert-email credentials self-provision; the owner is never sent to an installer. (1) cytech_register_email.sh: a press on a unit whose SMTP creds are not there yet now returns 'Alert emails are still finishing setup on this system -- this finishes automatically. Please press Register again in a few minutes.' The previous 'ask your installer to finish the email setup' text was a dead end for a freshly re-imaged unit (customer report 2026-10-15: the image predates the private-repo token, so the credentials never arrive and the owner had no path forward). (2) reset.sh: capture-time guard -- a refuse-to-capture ERROR when /config/.cytech_secrets lacks CYTECH_SECRETS_TOKEN, because clones from such an image could never set up owner alert email and nothing on a clone can fetch the token afterwards. (3) packages/cytech.yaml and cytech_alert_mail.py: comments only, wording brought in step. No first_boot.sh change was needed: ensure_smtp_credential (44d) already fetches USER/PASS from the private repo at every maintenance pass, and provisioning ends with one, so any unit whose .cytech_secrets carries the token self-heals with zero owner or operator action. Offline verification: yaml parse (pyyaml 6.0.3) OK; bash -n OK on both scripts; python ast OK. Bench verification: prior-copy reproduction + new-copy live check on ems.local 2026-10-16 (lettered round -- the functional file was installed in its committed bytes; no mirror deploy needed). T-A: stripped the token + SMTP creds + recipient from .cytech_secrets (byte-identical backup first) and pressed Register with the deployed copy -- the exact prior refusal appeared in both the result and popup files, rc=2 (the customer's report reproduced verbatim). Re-seeded only the token line and invoked shell_command.init_first_boot (the same call the HA-start automation makes; http=200) -- 'SMTP credential updated from private repo' appeared in the fresh log within ~20 s (line 360) and the pass ended exit 0; Register dry-run then reported creds=OK. Zero owner/operator action beyond the token. T-B: installed the committed register script (md5 0e84adaef8aefc3a8a41e849a1277d69) live and pressed Register on the no-creds unit -- the new message verbatim in both files, rc=2; then a full byte-identical restore (secrets cmp-verified against the pre-round backup, script back to 12afc1670f29d6f058585867c36842bb), popup file removed, notification cytech_register_result dismissed (http=200), final dry-run creds=OK. Residual gap, deliberate: an already-running unit from a pre-token image (like the reporting customer's) cannot self-heal -- the token must be hand-seeded once during remote support, after which the same maintenance fetch finishes the job; every image captured from a fixed master self-heals automatically.
